text:
sam: Heads up — saw a ~3x CPU increase on host-proxy after the 03:20 canary. p99 decode+serialize latency spiked, and syscall rate jumped way up.
perf-bot: alert: host-proxy cpu > 75% (2m) — group: eng-runtime — check 3250017876
maya: ugh, I saw that in the dashboard too. traces show a lot of tiny write syscalls from the streaming path.
sam: here's a short top-of-pprof (sampling over 30s) from the hot host:```\n(pprof) top\nSamples: 120  of 30 @ 0.25s\n      38  31.7%  31.7%  sys_writev\n      22  18.3%  50.0%  ingress::stream_frame_serialize\n      14  11.7%  61.7%  grpc::net::write_small\n      10   8.3%  70.0%  tokenizer::emit_token\n       8   6.7%  76.7%  kv_cache::lookup_miss\n```\njordan: interesting — `kv_cache::lookup_miss` is showing up. are we getting more cache misses for the micro requests?
eli: logs correlate: short requests (<200B) have ~3x more KV misses. Might be because we do per-chunk metadata lookups when `emit_token` fires.
maya: hypothesis: combination of (1) tokenizer producing lots of tiny frames, (2) gRPC proxy sending many small writev syscalls (no coalescing), and (3) per-chunk KV lookups causing blocking/fs/syscall churn. net effect = syscall storm + CPU spend in write path.
sam: repro steps I used:```bash
# synthetic: many tiny streaming requests
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  grpcurl -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -plaintext host-proxy:8080 inference.Service/StreamGen >/dev/null &
done
wait
```\njordan: tried a `wrk` style burst with 1k concurrent tiny POSTs and saw same p99 uplift. disabling `tcp_nodelay` on the proxy reduced syscalls by ~30% but added 4–5ms latency on p50.
eli: quick metric: kv cache hit-rate per-request-size (last 1h): `<200B: 65% , 200-1k: 87%, >1k: 94%` — so very small requests indeed hit more misses.
maya: two short-term mitigations: (A) enable small-write coalescing buffer in the proxy (collect up to ~4k/1ms), (B) add a lightweight in-process KV read cache (per-connection) to cut miss penalty for micro-requests. both low-risk to try.
sam: long-term: improve batching heuristics in runtime so we avoid emitting per-token frames for single-token responses and surface a micro-batch mode for chat-edges. also consider tuning gRPC initial window and SETTINGS to reduce CONTROL frame noise.
jordan: I can prototype the proxy writev coalesce PR today — quick patch: buffer until either size >= 4k or deadline 800us then flush. will run perf A/B.
eli: I'll add instrumentation: per-request KV hit/miss tag + emit sample traces that link to syscalls count. want to validate if misses cause sync I/O or just CPU.
maya: I'll flip on local coalesce and run canary; also try `SO_SNDBUF` + writev to see kernel coalescing behavior.
sam: action items: jordan -> PR for coalesce (ETA EOD), eli -> KV hit instrumentation (ETA 6h), maya -> canary config + kernel tuning experiment (ETA 3h). we'll regroup in #eng-runtime 1PM PT.
jordan: noted. will also run the `tcp_nodelay` toggle matrix and post results.
eli: quick note — if we do per-connection in-proc mini-cache, think about eviction/size; micro-requests are transient but very hot for certain customers. probably 32–64 entries LRU.
maya: agreed. keep it simple first.
sam: thanks all. tagging @maya @jordan @eli — pls paste traces/pprof in the thread. :mag: :thumbsup:
perf-bot: note: follow-up reminder scheduled at 3250021400
maya: copied. starting canary now.
jordan: starting proto PR run.
eli: adding KV tags to traces now.
sam: ok closing out for now — we'll update when canary results in. :white_check_mark:
